basis: Mitochondrial metabolic myopathy explicitly restricted to skeletal muscle; ophthalmoplegia and ptosis are occasional, not evidence of common ocular damage.
Localized infection of an eyelash follicle and adjacent eyelid glands; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Congenital abnormal origin of a pulmonary artery from the ductus arteriosus; pulmonary arteries belong to the cardiovascular axis.
Benign tumor originating in the sphenoid sinus; paranasal sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis.
B-cell lymphoma originating in skin; lymphoid blood-cell malignancy and lymphoma mechanism apply.
Genetic subtype of immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease; intestinal inflammation defines the disease.
Carcinoma of exocrine pancreatic acinar cells; metastatic sites are separately coded, and lipase-associated fat necrosis occurs in a minority.
Malignancy originating in the posterior urethra; the renal axis includes the entire urinary tract.
Pathogen-defined infectious umbrella; no anatomical site is specified for the group.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with profound intellectual disability and seizures; tube feeding does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage.
Intraductal papillomatosis conventionally denotes multiple breast duct papillomas, supported by the supplied child; breast has no axis.
Degenerative disease of the peripheral cornea.
Defined by an acute, reversible loss of memory function; its primary affected function is neurologic despite absence of an associated neurologic disorder.
PINK1-related neurodegenerative parkinsonism; urinary urgency does not demonstrate direct urinary tract damage.
Osteolysis, arthropathy and subcutaneous nodules define the spectrum; cardiovascular abnormalities occur in 30-79% by HPO, though individual defects are less frequent.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain metabolic defect; neurologic damage includes ataxia in 3/3 and cerebellar vermis atrophy in 2/2 reported patients.
Congenital common arterial trunk and interrupted aortic arch are structural cardiovascular malformations.
Endocrine pancreatic insulin dysregulation causes hypoglycemia; permanent neurologic injury is not established as a defining or sufficiently common manifestation here.
Proline metabolism defect; HPO reports seizures, intellectual disability and developmental delay in 80-99%, despite often-benign description. Renal insufficiency is only 5-29%.
Primary microcephaly with intellectual disability in 10/10 and simplified cerebral gyration in 2/2; cranial shape reflects abnormal brain development.
Proliferative cerebral vasculopathy causes destructive brain malformation; fixed joint contractures occur in 6/7 and talipes in 5/7 patients.
Hereditary motor-system disease defined by spastic paraplegia and extrapyramidal dysfunction; spasticity does not establish primary muscle damage.
Innate immunodeficiency with disseminated BCG infection; persistent Th2-associated airway disease occurred in 1/1 reported patient. Eosinophilia alone adds no blood-organ damage.
Progressive epileptic encephalopathy; optic atrophy in 3/3 HPO cases supports ocular damage, although this conflicts with the definition excluding neuro-ophthalmic findings.
Renal tubular acid-handling defect defines an acid-base disorder; rickets and hearing loss are not established as common across the umbrella.
